question: An infrastructure architect is analyzing the deployment type for an application. Several companies must be able to operate the application environment and integrate it with a third-party protocol. The development team also must have maximum control over their development environment, including the operating system used, Python interpreter, and corresponding libraries. Which cloud deployment solution meets those requirements?
options: private cloud Platform as a Service
public cloud Storage as a Service
hybrid cloud Software as a Service
community cloud Infrastructure as a Service
theory: A community cloud is shared among multiple organizations that need to jointly operate an environment (e.g., integrating a shared third-party protocol), while IaaS gives the customer the deepest level of control over the underlying OS, interpreter versions, and libraries — exactly what the development team needs. Combining these, a community-cloud IaaS deployment satisfies both the multi-company operational requirement and the maximum-developer-control requirement, unlike PaaS/SaaS models that abstract away OS-level control, or private/ public/hybrid models that don't match the "several companies jointly operate" requirement as directly. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 5 — Cloud Deployment and Service Models)
